what_its_for: Apraclonidine is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is used to treat or prevent high eye pressure (called intraocular pressure), which can occur in conditions like glaucoma or after certain eye procedures such as laser eye surgery.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using these eye drops. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and gently squeeze the prescribed number of drops into that pocket. Close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes and press gently on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with your finger. This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces the chance of it getting into your bloodstream. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, fingers, or any surface, as this can contaminate the drops. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) up to 3 times per day, or as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different depending on your condition. Space your doses evenly throughout the day, such as every 8 hours if taking 3 times daily.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store apraclonidine eye drops at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Protect it from light by keeping it in the original carton. Do not freeze the drops. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date and discard the bottle if it has expired or if the solution has changed color or become cloudy.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects your vision, as it may cause temporary blurred vision or drowsiness. Do not wear contact lenses while using these drops unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to prevent contamination. Tell your doctor if you are taking medications for blood pressure, depression (especially MAO inhibitors), or heart conditions, as apraclonidine can interact with these drugs. Avoid using other eye drops at the same time without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe eye pain, redness, or irritation that gets worse; sudden vision changes or vision loss; signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, severe rash, or difficulty breathing; very slow or irregular heartbeat; feeling faint or very dizzy; unusual paleness; severe headache; or significant eye discharge. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or if they get worse while using this medication.
when_it_works: Apraclonidine starts working within 1 hour of using the drops, and its peak effect on lowering eye pressure is usually seen within 3 to 5 hours. You may not feel any different when the medication is working because high eye pressure usually does not cause noticeable symptoms. Your doctor will check your eye pressure at follow-up visits to make sure the medication is working properly.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as its safety in these situations is not fully established. Children: This medication is not typically recommended for children. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medication. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. Heart or blood vessel disease: Use with caution if you have a history of heart disease, stroke, or circulation problems. Always tell your doctor about all medical conditions and medications you are taking before starting apraclonidine.
